clue.text: Senior officer and I hail RAF marches on manoeuvres

indicators.note: troops on manoeuvres move about and regroup, so the letters before it are redeployed

parts.note: fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A top commander salutes as the air force parades past on an exercise.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the most senior rank in the Royal Air Force below marshal of the force, a high-ranking commander.

clue.text: A dispute right off in public sale

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: something that is off has been taken away, so the right is removed from the dispute

parts.note: a ruction is a noisy row or quarrel
R is the usual abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A row breaks out and fairness is lost at a public sale.
explanation.walkthrough: A ruction minus its R leaves UCTION, which follows A to give AUCTION.
explanation.definitionFit: An auction is a sale open to all comers where goods go to the highest bidder.

clue.text: Launch posh car with final part not seen in public

indicators.note: if the last bit cannot be seen it has been dropped from the end of the car's name

parts.note: a Rolls, short for Rolls-Royce, is the classic luxury car
something out is openly known or seen

explanation.surface: A luxury car is unveiled to the public with its rear end hidden.
explanation.walkthrough: Rolls is everyday British shorthand for a Rolls-Royce, the byword for a posh car.
explanation.definitionFit: A rollout is the introduction of a new product or service to the market, its launch.

clue.text: Slam troubled land embracing distasteful and ultimately obsolete emblem

indicators.note: to embrace is to wrap your arms around, so the shuffled letters go round the next piece
something troubled is disturbed, so the word land is stirred up into a new order

parts.note: to hammer is to criticise severely, to slam
taken as written, to be rearranged
sick humour is distasteful

indicators.note: ultimately points to the very end, so only the final letter of the following word is used

parts.note: the last letter of obsolete

explanation.surface: A critic attacks a troubled country for its distasteful, outdated symbol.
explanation.walkthrough: The shuffled land is split in two, with the distasteful word sitting between its pieces; obsolete is a fair hint, since the Soviet symbol now belongs to history.
explanation.definitionFit: The crossed tools were the symbol of Soviet communism, so the phrase names a famous political badge.

clue.text: Grounds for believing study going into European depravity

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for European

indicators.note: going into something means entering it, so the study sits inside the word for depravity

parts.note: vice is wickedness or depravity
a den is a private room for work, a study

explanation.surface: A scholar researches European moral corruption to find reasons for faith.
explanation.definitionFit: Evidence is the facts or information that support a belief or show it to be true.

clue.text: Lord's house that's said to show style

indicators.note: said means the word is spoken rather than written, so its sound is what counts

parts.note: a manor is a lord's country estate and its house

explanation.surface: A nobleman's mansion is said to display good taste.
explanation.definitionFit: Manner is a way of doing something, a person's mode or fashion of behaving.

clue.text: Precinct with one tree adapted for emergency facility?

indicators.note: adapted means altered to suit a new purpose, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A town square with a single tree is converted into a disaster shelter.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark marks the definition as an example: such a centre is one kind of emergency facility.
explanation.definitionFit: A reception centre houses refugees or evacuees arriving after a disaster, a place for crisis care.

clue.text: Shock coverage?

parts.note: surface reading: news reporting of a startling event
setter's reading: a shock is a thick mass of hair, and this item covers it

explanation.walkthrough: Shock as a mane of hair, not a surprise, and coverage as something worn over it.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine mesh worn over the head keeps a mass of hair in place, literally covering it.

clue.text: Lavish bill to be settled — about time

indicators.note: about means around, so the rearranged letters surround the period of time
settling something puts it in order, so the letters of the bill are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: An extravagant invoice must be paid sometime soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Settled' reads as paying the bill; it is the signal to rearrange it.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal can mean generous or plentiful, as in a liberal helping, so it matches lavish.

clue.text: South American doctor's put by pass needed by old Scotsman

parts.note: a col is a mountain pass
O is the abbreviation for old
MB is a medical degree, Bachelor of Medicine, so a doctor
Ian is the Scottish form of John, the crossword's stock Scotsman

explanation.surface: A medic is stationed by a mountain pass, waiting for an elderly Scot.
explanation.definitionFit: A Colombian comes from Colombia, a country in the north-west of South America.

clue.text: Get up with cold leg?

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold on taps
a leg is one example of a limb

explanation.surface: Getting out of bed with a chilly leg.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark signals that leg is defining a limb by example.
explanation.definitionFit: To climb is to go up, ascend, so it matches get up in the sense of mounting.

clue.text: Combined chant after time passes

indicators.note: when something passes it goes away, so the time letter leaves the chant

parts.note: to intone is to chant in a monotone
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A group chant rings out after time runs on.
explanation.walkthrough: INTONE without its T gives IN ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something all in one unites several parts or functions together, so the phrase means combined.

clue.text: This writer pronounced batsman to be startling phenomenon

indicators.note: pronounced means spoken, so the writer's word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: this writer is the setter, who would say I
an opener is a batsman who starts a cricket innings

explanation.surface: A columnist declares a cricketer a stunning sensation.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the opening batsmen face the first balls of an innings.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-opener is a revelation, something surprising that changes how you see things.

clue.text: Greek character gets straw matting for bird

parts.note: nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
thatch is a roof covering of woven straw or reeds

explanation.surface: A Greek gets straw matting to line a bird's nest.
explanation.definitionFit: The nuthatch is a small woodland songbird that climbs tree trunks head first.

clue.text: Firearm recoiled many times, used by investigator

parts.note: PI stands for private investigator

indicators.note: to recoil is to spring back, so the words for many times run backwards

parts.note: lots of times means many times

explanation.surface: A detective's gun kicked back repeatedly in use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Recoiled' wants to describe the gun firing, but it is the signal to read backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A pistol is a small handgun, a kind of firearm held in one hand.

clue.text: Flat, perhaps — small verbal joke that's unsophisticated

parts.note: a flat is one example of a home
S is the abbreviation for small
a pun is a play on words

explanation.surface: A dull, small wordplay gag lacks any polish.
explanation.walkthrough: Flat looks like an adjective meaning dull; it is the noun for an apartment.
explanation.definitionFit: Homespun originally meant cloth woven at home, hence plain, simple and lacking refinement.

clue.text: Stay with two bridge players in trip

indicators.note: in places the bridge players inside the word for a trip

parts.note: a ride is a short journey or trip
East and South are two of the four bridge seats, E and S

explanation.surface: Two card players travel together and settle in for a while.
explanation.walkthrough: RIDE holds ES as R(ES)IDE.
explanation.definitionFit: To reside is to live or dwell somewhere, to stay there as a home.

clue.text: Mechanical corrosion overwhelms old boy in charge

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf, so the word for corrosion swallows the old boy

parts.note: rot is decay or corrosion
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: Rust spreads over a former pupil who is running the works.
explanation.walkthrough: An old boy is a former pupil of a British school.
explanation.definitionFit: Robotic means like a robot, moving in a stiff, automatic way, so it equals mechanical.

clue.text: Lad must limit desire to be performer in theatre

indicators.note: to limit is to hem in, so the lad's word encloses the desire

parts.note: a son is a boy, a lad
an urge is a strong desire

explanation.surface: A boy has to curb his ambition to go on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: The theatre here is the operating theatre of a hospital, not a playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon carries out operations in a hospital operating theatre, so a performer there.

clue.text: Fantastic tenor and another briefly entering company, source of music

parts.note: CO is the abbreviation for company

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so the letters go into the company
something fantastic is wild and fanciful, so the voice's letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
another tenor, abbreviated as T

explanation.surface: Two singers join a firm whose star tenor is wonderful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another briefly' means a second tenor cut to its abbreviation, T, as on a choral score.
explanation.definitionFit: A cornetto is an old wooden wind instrument, the cornett, so it is a thing that makes music.

clue.text: Bill with a cost largely obscured for sauce

indicators.note: largely means mostly but not wholly, so the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a tab is a bill, as in picking up the tab

indicators.note: obscured means muddled and hard to make out, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
cost without its final letter

explanation.surface: A restaurant bill hides most of the price of the sauce.
explanation.definitionFit: Tabasco is a trademarked hot pepper sauce from Louisiana, a fiery condiment.

clue.text: Given command, soldiers act to overcome resistance

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers

indicators.note: to overcome is to get on top of and round, so the act encloses the resistance

parts.note: a deed is an act
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: Under orders, troops move to crush the opposition.
explanation.walkthrough: OR, other ranks, means soldiers who are not officers.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordered means instructed or told to do something, as when a command has been given.

clue.text: Seasoned food served up in Lima — lashings!

indicators.note: in a down clue, served up means the letters climb, reading bottom to top
in says the letters sit inside the following words

parts.note: the letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Spiced food dished up in Peru's capital in great quantities.
explanation.walkthrough: Lashings is British slang for plenty, as in lashings of ginger beer.
explanation.definitionFit: Salami is a cured sausage flavoured with garlic and spices, a seasoned cold meat.

clue.text: Playwright encapsulating rogue fence

indicators.note: to encapsulate is to enclose in a capsule, so the dramatist's name surrounds the rogue

parts.note: J M Barrie wrote Peter Pan
a cad is a dishonourable man, a rogue

explanation.surface: A dramatist sums up a rascal who deals in stolen goods.
explanation.walkthrough: Fence looks like the criminal receiver suggested by rogue; it is a barrier. BARRIE holds CAD as BARRI(CAD)E.
explanation.definitionFit: A barricade is a makeshift barrier blocking a way, much as a fence keeps people out.

clue.text: Place in military unit journalist holding award

indicators.note: holding means gripping around, so the journalist surrounds the award

parts.note: ED is short for editor, the stock journalist
MBE, Member of the Order of the British Empire, is a British honour

explanation.surface: A decorated reporter is attached to an army regiment.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition runs to 'unit': journalists embedded with troops in war zones.
explanation.definitionFit: To embed a reporter is to attach them to a fighting unit so they cover a war from inside it.

clue.text: Modify introduction to text lacking force

indicators.note: an introduction comes at the start, so only the opening letter of the next word is used

parts.note: the first letter of text
weak means lacking strength or force

explanation.surface: An editor revises a feeble opening to a piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: To tweak is to make a small adjustment, a fine-tuning change to something.

clue.text: An early form of fuel?

parts.note: surface reading: a primitive type of energy source such as wood or coal
setter's reading: food is fuel for the body, and this is what you eat first in a meal

explanation.walkthrough: Early means at the start of dinner, not in history, and fuel is food.
explanation.definitionFit: A starter dish served before the main course, a small bite to whet the appetite.

clue.text: None conceived of new-fangled burger, say

indicators.note: something newfangled has been made over in a novel way, so the letters are refashioned

parts.note: fifteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Nobody dreamt up this modern fast-food patty.
explanation.definitionFit: A burger is one example of quick, pre-prepared or takeaway food made for ease rather than cooking.
